sample_unit: AI-generated clinic notes evaluated by physicians

links.outcome: Errors in AI drafted notes with potential for serious harm if not corrected
links.effect: 19 (5.3%) notes contained errors rated serious or imminent risk (severity 4-5); 14.9% (143/960) of notes left entirely unedited.
links.quote: However, because a small number contained errors that carried the risk of serious harm if not corrected, careful clinician review of notes remains imperative.

links.outcome: Local assessment of ambient scribe documentation accuracy and quality via physician review of notes
links.effect: Local pilot review of 356 notes identified error types and severity; 94.7% (337/356) free from significant errors, showing feasibility of local evaluation.
links.quote: Prior to deploying an AI scribe, organizations should pilot the technology and include an efficient review process to understand the nature and type of errors common at their organization.

links.outcome: Physician editing rates of AI-generated notes as a reliance signal
links.effect: Median 9.0% (IQR 2.5%-21.9%) of AI words changed; 14.9% (143/960) notes unedited; physician average edit ranged 1.9% to 69.3%.
links.quote: Physician editing practices varied widely, with average percentages of AI-generated words changed ranging from 1.9% to 69.3% (median 9.0%, IQR 2.5%-21.9%).

screen.reason: This prospective pilot study evaluates the quality, safety risks, and physician editing behaviors of an ambient generative AI scribe deployed in real-world clinical practice across 31 physicians.

primary.practice: clinician review and quality auditing of AI notes
